subject: Priority entitlement for Sprint Epsilon — temporary elastic headroom request
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priority entitlement for Sprint Epsilon — temporary elastic headroom request

Team —

Quick context: NextWave (pilot customer) is running a live usability pilot the week of June 15. Their load testing this morning showed an expected 6–8x token-per-minute spike for ~48–72 hours during the initial public-facing demo window. This is a sales-critical pilot — if the demo struggles we will likely lose a multi-quarter deal.

Ask: can we provision a temporary "elastic headroom" entitlement against the Dedicated GPU pool (region: us-west-2) for their pilot window? Ideally this is a soft-reservation that sits above current autoscale thresholds and only gets used for real customer traffic. High-level requirements:
- Duration: 2026-06-14 00:00 UTC -> 2026-06-17 23:59 UTC (72 hours)
- Estimate: ~1,800 GPU-minutes total (spike pattern, not sustained) — equivalent to a small burst lane of ~2x their normal slice
- Rollback: automatic removal at window end, with an ops-led rollback checklist if we see sustained usage beyond the window

What I need from you: feasibility and a short runbook (who does what, billing implications, guardrails) by EOD Monday so I can confirm with NextWave and update contracts. Attached a small capacity plan I put together (epsilon_capacity_plan.xlsx).

If there's a policy blocker, call it out — we can propose a short contract addendum or one-off surcharge.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Sales Lead, Enterprise 
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0199

Attachments: epsilon_capacity_plan.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priority entitlement for Sprint Epsilon — temporary elastic headroom request

Vanessa — thanks for the heads up and the attachment. A few quick clarifying questions before we scope the runbook:
1) Can you confirm the expected average sequence length and tokens/sec during the spike? That changes how we model KV cache pressure.
2) Is NextWave ok with a short-term pricing addendum for the extra reserved headroom (we usually do a one-off surcharge for emergency carve-outs)?
3) Do they require a hard SLA on the headroom or is a best-effort buffered lane acceptable?

Operationally two alternatives I want to flag:
- Soft elastic headroom (your ask): fastest to approve, low infra churn, we bill as a discrete overage.
- Canary variant routing: deploy a quantized/faster model variant to the canary lane for the demo window to reduce per-token cost and pressure (requires model + engineering work, ~3–5 days).

If Laura/Marcus confirm feasibility for a soft-headroom path we should also document a brief test plan (smoke test + failover) and a post-mortem ask. I can help draft the short contract wording once we have numbers.

—Kimberly
Director, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priority entitlement for Sprint Epsilon — temporary elastic headroom request

On Sat, May 30, 2026 at 11:04 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Vanessa — thanks for the heads up and the attachment. A few quick clarifying questions before we scope the runbook:
> 1) Can you confirm the expected average sequence length and tokens/sec during the spike? That changes how we model KV cache pressure.
> 2) Is NextWave ok with a short-term pricing addendum for the extra reserved headroom (we usually do a one-off surcharge for emergency carve-outs)?
> 3) Do they require a hard SLA on the headroom or is a best-effort buffered lane acceptable?

Team — operational plan below; I ran a quick cluster projection based on Vanessa's estimates and the attached workbook. TL;DR: we can do a controlled soft-reservation for the requested window with the following constraints and tasks.

Proposal (ops):
- Provision an ephemeral "expedited headroom" slice on Pool-USW2-08 (pool id: 08). This will be a soft reservation that sets an upper autoscale limit + a policy guard to prevent eviction of the pilot's workloads during the window.
- Config: set temporary autoscale upper bound = current upper * 1.8 (matches Vanessa's burst estimate). Add a 20-minute cool-down to avoid oscillation.
- Safety: overflow routing to fallback model variant in the eu-west-1 mirror region to protect shared capacity if we exceed expected usage.
- Billing: tag usage to billing code NW-EPSILON-TRIAL and create a one-off invoice line for the spike usage. Finance needs to approve surcharge; Dev (cc'd) can assist with billing code creation.
- Runbook (attached): infra_runbook_expedited_headroom.md — includes step-by-step for provisioning, smoke test, escalation path and rollback.

Tasks & owners:
- Laura: create pool-slice, apply policy, run smoke test (ETA: Wed 06/10 EOD)
- Marcus: implement fallback routing and health checks (ETA: Thu 06/11)
- Dev: create billing code and coordinate finance approval (ETA: Tue 06/09)
- Kimberly: finalize contract addendum language for surcharge (ETA: Mon 06/08)
- Vanessa: confirm dates with NextWave and share acceptance to proceed (ETA: Mon 06/08)

Risk notes: if load is higher than projected we will hit cross-pool throttles; fallback to eu mirror will add latency. If NextWave needs a guaranteed hard SLA we will need a larger reserved commitment and a different commercial path.

I attached the runbook and a short checklist. Happy to run the smoke test with you — let's schedule a 30-min dry-run on Thu 06/11 morning.

—Laura
Head of Infra & Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: infra_runbook_expedited_headroom.md

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Thanks everyone — this looks good and I approve the expedited headroom plan. I looped in Sanjay and contracts so they see the proposed dates and billing code flow. Sanjay, are you ok with the proposed window (Jun 14–17) and the billing approach (one-off surcharge on code NW-EPSILON-TRIAL)? If yes, I will send an addendum this week so we can lock seats.

I also want to confirm we run the smoke test on Thu 06/11 09:00 PT (Laura / Marcus / Dev / me). Please confirm availability.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — this makes the pilot much less risky.

Vanessa Ortiz
